grade.first_issue: In the termination argument, the asserted change in the sum of squares is false. Writing a=min(e_p,f_p) and b=max(e_p,f_p), the actual decrease is a²+b²-[a²+(b-a)²]=2ab-a²=a(2b-a), not 2a(b-a). This calculation is load-bearing for the monovariant argument, so Rule C caps the score at 5, although it is repaired by a one-line correction.
grade.summary: The claimed terminal value and the primewise gcd invariant are correct, and the overall strategy proves both requested statements after correcting the monovariant calculation. The submission notices and separately handles the equal-exponent case, but its false displayed formula remains the only justification for strict decrease when the shared positive exponents are unequal. Thus the proof is not correct as submitted, though the repair is immediate and preserves the entire strategy.
strengths: Correctly analyzes how the number of entries greater than 1 changes and shows it never becomes zero.
Uses an appropriate finite sum-of-squares monovariant together with the count of non-unit entries.
Correctly identifies the valuation transformation as (e,f)↦(min(e,f),|e-f|).
Correctly proves invariance of the gcd of the p-adic valuations and reconstructs the unique terminal value.

errors.description: The displayed formula for ΔΦ_p is algebraically incorrect. Because it supplies the justification for monotonicity in a central termination proof, it is a false load-bearing statement under Rule C, even though replacing it by ΔΦ_p=min(e_p,f_p)(2max(e_p,f_p)−min(e_p,f_p)) completes the proof directly.
